title: Lesson 4: Framing Value and ROI: How to Talk to a Buyer, Not a Builder
description: The craft of turning what an agent does into a number a buyer can defend: how to measure value honestly, build ROI math that survives scrutiny, and talk outcomes instead of features to the person who signs the check.

questions.question: How should a consultant translate a capability for a buyer?
options: Describe each feature in technical terms and let the buyer map it
Convert the capability into the buyer's own units
Lead with the architecture so the buyer trusts the engineering
Quote the capability in tokens and response times
questions.explanation: A buyer asks what the capability does for them, so the consultant restates it in the buyer's own units, such as hours, errors, and money.

questions.question: Which ROI mistake most damages a consultant's credibility?
options: Quoting a range so wide it covers every outcome
Naming the success metric after the deal instead of before it
Pricing from the numbers gathered during discovery
Claiming the agent replaces the whole job
questions.explanation: An ROI case collapses when it claims more than the agent actually changes; claim only the routine slice and count human review as a cost.

questions.question: Why does honest framing put the recurring running cost in the math up front?
options: Hiding it until the buyer finds it destroys trust
Running costs are too small to matter to the total
Buyers almost never examine ongoing expenses
The build price already includes all future costs
questions.explanation: A running agent carries ongoing costs, and hiding them until the buyer discovers them destroys the trust an honest, still-positive net would have earned.
